events.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' quarterly inflation report, the single most important domestic data point for the Reserve Bank of Australia's rate decisions. This morning's print came in at 4.0% year on year, a touch below the 4.1% consensus and down slightly from the first quarter, with the trimmed mean core measure also easing. A softer than expected read takes some pressure off the RBA ahead of its mid-August meeting.

events.event: Bank of Canada Summary of Deliberations
events.description: A written account of the discussion behind the Bank of Canada's most recent rate decision, published roughly two weeks after the meeting. It can reveal how divided or confident the Governing Council was, which matters for how markets price the next move.

The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) announces its target range for the US federal funds rate. This is one of the single biggest drivers of the US dollar and global markets: a surprise move, or surprise language in the statement, can cause sharp swings across all major currency pairs.

The Fed Chair takes questions from reporters straight after the rate decision. Often more market-moving than the decision itself, since this is where the Fed explains its reasoning and gives clues about what comes next.

Japan's headline Consumer Price Index, measuring the change in prices for a typical basket of goods and services. A key input for the Bank of Japan's policy decisions, and released just ahead of this week's BoJ meeting.

A monthly measure of the volume of goods sold by retailers in the Eurozone's largest economy. Since German consumer spending accounts for a big share of Eurozone demand, a surprise here can move the euro ahead of the bloc-wide growth and inflation figures due later the same morning.
An early estimate of quarterly economic growth in Germany, the Eurozone's largest economy. Often moves the euro ahead of the full Eurozone GDP figure released later the same morning.

An early estimate of quarterly economic growth across the whole Eurozone. One of the most closely watched growth indicators for the euro, as it feeds directly into the ECB's outlook for the bloc, coming after a contraction in the first quarter.
A public speech by Philip Lane, the ECB's Chief Economist. His remarks are watched particularly closely as he's seen as a bellwether for the Governing Council's internal economic thinking.

events.event: Bank of England interest rate decision
events.description: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) announces its decision on Bank Rate, the UK's main interest rate. Money markets currently price around an 86% chance of a hold, with the rest priced for a surprise hike to 4.00%, following June's split 7-2 vote and hawkish signals from Chief Economist Huw Pill. A surprise decision or shift in the vote split can move sterling sharply.

events.event: BoE Monetary Policy Report & Financial Stability Report
events.description: Published alongside the rate decision, this sets out the Bank's updated forecasts for inflation and growth, plus its assessment of risks to the UK financial system. Markets read this for clues on the future path of rates.

The Governor of the Bank of England answers questions from journalists straight after the rate decision. Often the moment that moves sterling most, as it's where the Bank explains its reasoning in its own words.
An early estimate of German inflation, released ahead of the full Eurozone inflation figure. As the bloc's largest economy, Germany's number often sets the tone for how the euro reacts the next day.

The first official estimate of US economic growth for the quarter. A core input into how the Fed and markets judge the health of the world's largest economy: surprises here tend to move the dollar broadly, and land just a day after the Fed's own decision.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation. Often more market-moving than CPI because of how directly it feeds into the Fed's own policy framework.

The number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time that week. A high-frequency, early read on the US labour market; usually a minor mover unless it deviates sharply from expectations.

China's official, government-compiled gauge of manufacturing activity, released on the last day of the month. A reading above 50 signals expansion; below signals contraction. One of the more closely watched early signals of Chinese economic health, which matters for AUD and NZD as much as CNY given trade links.

events.event: Bank of Japan interest rate decision
events.description: The Bank of Japan announces its target for short-term interest rates, alongside its quarterly Outlook Report. Following the BoJ's recent shift toward tighter policy, each decision is watched closely for signs of further rate rises, which tend to strengthen the yen. A Reuters poll of economists found the large majority expect a further 25 basis point hike by the end of the year.

A monthly composite leading indicator for the Swiss economy from the KOF Swiss Economic Institute, pointing to likely activity over the next six months. A widely watched gauge of Swiss business sentiment, though it typically moves the franc less than a central bank event would.

The BoJ Governor explains the decision and answers questions from the press. Often moves the yen more than the decision itself, particularly any comments on the pace of future policy normalisation and the timing of the next hike.

An early estimate of Eurozone-wide inflation for the month. One of the key inputs into the ECB's interest rate decisions, and a regular source of euro volatility on release. Core inflation, which strips out food and energy, is expected to hold steady at 2.4%.

The percentage of the Eurozone workforce that is unemployed. A slower-moving indicator that rarely surprises markets, but still forms part of the broader picture of Eurozone economic health, with the rate recently sitting at a record low.

events.event: Canada GDP by industry (May, with June advance estimate)
events.description: Statistics Canada's monthly measure of economic output by industry. Released with a roughly two-month lag, it gives an early read on how the Canadian economy is tracking heading into the third quarter.
A regional survey of purchasing managers in the Chicago area, used as an early signal for the following week's national ISM manufacturing survey. Usually a modest, secondary market mover.

A private-sector survey of Chinese manufacturing activity, skewed toward smaller, export- and tech-oriented firms, released a few days after the official NBS PMI. Often diverges from the official gauge and is watched as a cross-check on the health of China's factory sector, with knock-on relevance for AUD and NZD.

Switzerland's headline inflation reading from the Federal Statistical Office. With Swiss inflation running well below other major economies, this feeds directly into the SNB's assessment of whether its current policy stance remains appropriate.

The final, revised reading of S&P Global's Eurozone manufacturing survey, usually only a small adjustment from the flash estimate published earlier in the month. A confirmation-style release that rarely moves the euro much on its own.
The final, revised reading of S&P Global's UK manufacturing survey. Like its Eurozone counterpart, this is usually a modest revision to the flash figure and a secondary mover for sterling.

The Institute for Supply Management's survey of US manufacturing activity, released on the first business day of the month. A reading above 50 signals expansion. Watched as an early, broad-based signal of US industrial health for the month just ended.

The Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, a measure of unfilled positions across the US economy that the Federal Reserve watches closely as a gauge of labour market slack. A drop toward levels seen before the pandemic would support the case for further Fed easing.

A broader measure of new orders placed with US manufacturers than the durable goods report released a few days earlier. Usually a secondary market mover, since much of the durable goods component is already known by the time this is published.
